_doc: Point-in-time fact sheet for PFE retrospectives (retro/build_pfe.py). Every value is tied to a source and becomes visible only on or after that source's 'published' date. A filing accepted after the 16:00 ET close is dated the next trading day ('filed' keeps the acceptance time, US Eastern; EDGAR gives only the filing date before 2003); the earnings 8-Ks of 2007-2009 were accepted before the open or during the session on their release days. The builder uses the latest history vintage published by AS_OF, the prints published by AS_OF that report a fiscal year after that history (a Q4 print reports the year just ended and extends the history until the 10-K), the guides for the current fiscal year (each field from the latest guide that states it) and the latest declared dividend. Pfizer's fiscal year is the calendar year (subsidiaries outside the U.S. close on November 30). EPS is GAAP diluted EPS from continuing operations; the company's adjusted EPS removes purchase-accounting amortization, which recurs, so it is shown and never used. 2003 is excluded and the history starts with 2004. Guides: reported diluted EPS ranges (the current-FY EPS) and revenue ranges in dollars, read as growth on the last full year in the history; Pfizer guides no quarter and no operating or pre-tax margin. A print's growth and margins are derived from the raw figures of its release ('raw', $ millions; the builder re-derives and checks them), each against the year-ago quarter as the same release shows it. Rule T's raw figures are in 'rule_t'. No later fact enters through this file: every source's published date bounds its use. From 2010: a Q4 print may restate the year before it on a new basis ('restates': its EPS and revenues from continuing operations), which replaces that year from the print until a 10-K vintage published after it carries the year; the reported diluted EPS guide is used as published, discontinued operations included where the guide includes them (the only EPS line Pfizer guides).

history_vintages.why: 'is a research-based, global pharmaceutical company. We discover, develop, manufacture and market leading prescription medicines for humans and animals' (FY2006 10-K, Item 1); 'Competition from manufacturers of generic drugs is a major challenge for us around the world. Upon the expiration or loss of patent protection for one of our products ... we can lose the major portion of sales of that product in a very short period' (Item 1A); Lipitor's U.S. basic product patent 'expires in March 2010', the enantiomer patent 'expires in June 2011' (both including the pediatric exclusivity period); 'Our businesses are conducted in intensely competitive and often highly regulated markets'

rule_t._doc: Rule T values behind the engine's signal thresholds (retro/README.md, 'PFE'): the decade of the FY2006 10-K, the vintage public on 2008-01-04, is fiscal 1997-2006. Each change comes from the latest 10-K published by then that reports both years: U.S. and international revenues (consolidated less United States) from the geographic data of its notes; the gross margin (revenues less cost of sales, which excludes the amortization of intangible assets) from its statement of income; total revenues and income from continuing operations before taxes from its financial summary. Seams stay as published: the FY1998 and FY1999 10-Ks report Pfizer before the Warner-Lambert pooling (1997 and 1998 changes); the FY2000 10-K onward pools it; revenue reclassifications (EITF 00-14 and 00-25) and the Consumer Healthcare discontinuance enter with the filings that made them; 2003 carries the Pharmacia purchase (inventory step-up in cost of sales, the $5,052M in-process R&D charge in pre-tax income). 'raw' holds the figures in $ millions; the builder re-derives each value and each threshold and refuses to build if they differ.

price_basis: Yahoo's PFE series is adjusted by a factor of 1.054 dated 2020-11-17 (Yahoo's split event for that date); every date here precedes it, so the builder multiplies Yahoo's close by it to restore the price as traded (2007-12-31 $22.73 and 2008-12-31 $17.71, the year-end market values per share in the FY2007 and FY2008 10-Ks). No Pfizer split after the 3-for-1 of 1999 precedes or restates any per-share fact in this file.
